# Ripe Reads

> Is this book ripe for my kid yet? First-person age-readiness ratings for popular romantasy and crossover fantasy, written for parents and librarians. Every rating is a judgment by one reader, stated plainly, with sources listed. Where I have not read a book myself the page says so.

## How to cite
Attribute ratings to "Ripe Reads" and link the book page. Ratings are opinions; the publisher's stated age (where it exists) is listed separately on every page.

## The rubric
Five signals, each scored 0–4. The age band is a judgment informed by the signals, not a formula.
- **Romance & heat** (romance): 0 = none; 1 = crushes and kisses; 2 = sensual, fade-to-black; 3 = on-page but not graphic; 4 = explicit on-page sex
- **Violence & gore** (violence): 0 = none; 1 = peril, bloodless; 2 = fights with injury; 3 = deaths, some gore; 4 = torture or sustained gore
- **Language** (language): 0 = clean; 1 = mild (damn, hell); 2 = occasional strong; 3 = frequent strong; 4 = pervasive strong
- **Substances** (substances): 0 = none; 1 = mentioned; 2 = social drinking; 3 = drunkenness or drugs on page; 4 = glamorised or central
- **Heavy themes** (themes): 0 = light; 1 = grief or loss; 2 = abuse, trauma, prejudice; 3 = sexual threat, self-harm; 4 = sustained or graphic

## Age bands
- 10–12 (stamp "10+", Middle school)
- 12–14 (stamp "12+", Middle school)
- 14–16 (stamp "14+", High school)
- 16–18 (stamp "16+", High school)
- 18+ (stamp "18+", Adult crossover)

## Read status
- "read": I have read the book; first-person experience appears on the page.
- "unmarked": rated from the publisher record, trade reviews and consistent reader reports; no first-person experience is claimed.

## Book page structure
Every book page has these ten sections in order: The short version · What it's about · Ripeness, signal by signal · Who it's ripe for · What the publisher says · Where it sits in the series · If this is too much · If they're ready for more · Lists this appears on · Sources & how I rated this

## Books
- [Fourth Wing by Rebecca Yarros](https://ripereads.example/books/fourth-wing/): ripe at 18+, signals 14/20, status read. An adult romantasy that teens are reading in huge numbers. The dragons and the war college are the hook; the explicit sex scenes are the reason I keep it at eighteen-plus rather than letting the cover art decide.
- [A Court of Thorns and Roses by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/a-court-of-thorns-and-roses/): ripe at 16+, signals 12/20, status read. A Beauty and the Beast retelling with real teeth. The first book alone sits at sixteen-plus for me: one on-page sex scene, a lot of sensuality, and a torture-heavy final third. The sequels are a different, more explicit conversation.
- [Powerless by Lauren Roberts](https://ripereads.example/books/powerless/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. A YA trials-and-prince romance that delivers the enemies-to-lovers banter teens want with the bedroom door firmly shut. Fourteen-plus for me, on violence and a drinking scene rather than heat.
- [Divine Rivals by Rebecca Ross](https://ripereads.example/books/divine-rivals/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status read. The gentlest romantasy on this shelf. Rival journalists, letters passed through a magic wardrobe, a war between gods happening just off the page. Twelve-plus, with the war scenes as the only real weight.
- [Legendborn by Tracy Deonn](https://ripereads.example/books/legendborn/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status read. Arthurian legend on a modern Southern campus, written with real anger about whose history gets to be magic. I put it at fourteen-plus for grief, racism and a bloody back half, not for romance, which stays at a slow simmer.
- [The Cruel Prince by Holly Black](https://ripereads.example/books/the-cruel-prince/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. Court politics in Faerie, narrated by a mortal girl who decides to be as ruthless as the people who raised her. I stamp it fourteen-plus: the cruelty is psychological as much as physical, and there is a lot of drinking.
- [Six of Crows by Leigh Bardugo](https://ripereads.example/books/six-of-crows/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. The best-built heist in young adult fiction, with a crew whose backstories carry the real weight. Fourteen-plus on violence and trauma; the romances are slow and the door stays closed.
- [Shadow and Bone by Leigh Bardugo](https://ripereads.example/books/shadow-and-bone/): ripe at 12+, signals 7/20, status read. Tsarist-flavoured fantasy about an orphan who turns out to be the one person who can destroy the darkness splitting her country. Twelve-plus. The romance is chaste and the villain is seductive in a way worth a conversation.
- [Caraval by Stephanie Garber](https://ripereads.example/books/caraval/): ripe at 12+, signals 7/20, status read. A dreamlike game-within-a-carnival where nothing is quite real and a sister needs rescuing. I put it at twelve-plus. The lushness is the appeal; an abusive father in the opening is the content to know about.
- [Serpent & Dove by Shelby Mahurin](https://ripereads.example/books/serpent-and-dove/): ripe at 16+, signals 14/20, status read. A witch forced to marry a witch hunter, in a French-flavoured city where witches burn. Sixteen-plus: an on-page sex scene, heavy language and a culture of public executions make it the oldest YA on this shelf.
- [An Ember in the Ashes by Sabaa Tahir](https://ripereads.example/books/an-ember-in-the-ashes/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. Roman-inspired military fantasy told by a slave and a soldier. I stamp it fourteen-plus, and the upper end of that: the violence is brutal and the threat of sexual violence is constant, even though it is never carried through on the page.
- [These Violent Delights by Chloe Gong](https://ripereads.example/books/these-violent-delights/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status read. Romeo and Juliet as rival gang heirs in 1926 Shanghai, with a monster in the river and a contagion that makes people claw their own throats. Fourteen-plus, on body horror rather than romance.
- [Belladonna by Adalyn Grace](https://ripereads.example/books/belladonna/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status read. A gothic murder mystery in which the heroine's love interest is Death himself. I put it at fourteen-plus for sensuality that pushes the YA line without crossing it, and for poisonings treated with relish.
- [The Atlas Six by Olivie Blake](https://ripereads.example/books/the-atlas-six/): ripe at 16+, signals 13/20, status read. Six brilliant, unpleasant magicians compete for five places in a secret society, and one of them will be eliminated. Adult-published, sixteen-plus for me: the sex is mostly off the page, the cruelty is not.
- [Lightlark by Alex Aster](https://ripereads.example/books/lightlark/): ripe at 12+, signals 5/20, status read. Six cursed realms, a hundred-day contest on a vanishing island, two love interests and a lot of twists. Twelve-plus. The romance is kisses and glances, the violence is brisk, and the prose is pitched young.
- [Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief by Rick Riordan](https://ripereads.example/books/percy-jackson-the-lightning-thief/): ripe at 10+, signals 3/20, status read. The gateway drug to fantasy for a whole generation, and I would hand it to a confident nine-year-old. Monsters, sarcasm, a boy who learns his ADHD and dyslexia are features. The only weight is an abusive stepfather and a missing mother.
- [Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone by J.K. Rowling](https://ripereads.example/books/harry-potter-and-the-sorcerers-stone/): ripe at 10+, signals 2/20, status read. The first book is a warm school story with a scary last act. I stamp it ten-plus and note that the series grows up with its reader, so approving book one is not approving book seven.
- [Keeper of the Lost Cities by Shannon Messenger](https://ripereads.example/books/keeper-of-the-lost-cities/): ripe at 10+, signals 3/20, status read. A telepathic twelve-year-old discovers she is an elf and leaves her human family behind. Ten-plus from me: friendship drama, a love triangle in slow motion, and a kidnapping are the whole of the weight.
- [Wings of Fire: The Dragonet Prophecy by Tui T. Sutherland](https://ripereads.example/books/wings-of-fire-the-dragonet-prophecy/): ripe at 10+, signals 5/20, status read. Dragons as protagonists, in a war that is not pretend. I put it at ten-plus, mainly because a dragon is killed in an arena and younger readers notice.
- [The School for Good and Evil by Soman Chainani](https://ripereads.example/books/the-school-for-good-and-evil/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status read. Two best friends are kidnapped to a school where fairy tales are trained, and each lands in the wrong half. Ten-plus from me; the satire is sharp, the peril is cartoonish, and the ending has a kiss that matters.
- [Nevermoor: The Trials of Morrigan Crow by Jessica Townsend](https://ripereads.example/books/nevermoor/): ripe at 10+, signals 2/20, status read. A cursed girl is whisked to a secret city and entered in trials for a magical society. I would hand this to a nine-year-old without a second thought; the villain is the only shadow.
- [Amari and the Night Brothers by B.B. Alston](https://ripereads.example/books/amari-and-the-night-brothers/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status read. Men in Black meets a magic school, led by a Black girl from the projects who refuses to be told what she is. Ten-plus from me, and one of the most confident middle grade debuts of recent years.
- [Aru Shah and the End of Time by Roshani Chokshi](https://ripereads.example/books/aru-shah-and-the-end-of-time/): ripe at 10+, signals 2/20, status read. Hindu mythology given the Percy Jackson treatment, with a heroine whose main power is lying. I stamp it ten-plus, and younger if the reader is already a Riordan fan.
- [Skandar and the Unicorn Thief by A.F. Steadman](https://ripereads.example/books/skandar-and-the-unicorn-thief/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status read. Unicorns reimagined as bloodthirsty war mounts that only bonded riders can control. I stamp it ten-plus; the unicorns are scary by design and the school story around them is warm.
- [Artemis Fowl by Eoin Colfer](https://ripereads.example/books/artemis-fowl/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status read. A twelve-year-old criminal mastermind kidnaps a fairy for ransom. Ten-plus from me: the violence is heist-movie slick, the hero is a villain, and the book knows it.
- [Eragon by Christopher Paolini](https://ripereads.example/books/eragon/): ripe at 12+, signals 7/20, status read. A farm boy, a dragon egg, an empire to topple. I put it at twelve-plus: the dragon bond is the appeal, and a torture scene and a village massacre are the weight.
- [The Hunger Games by Suzanne Collins](https://ripereads.example/books/the-hunger-games/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status read. Children killing children on television, written so that the horror is the point. Twelve-plus from me, and the right book at twelve for most readers; the romance is a performance and the violence is never fun.
- [Cinder by Marissa Meyer](https://ripereads.example/books/cinder/): ripe at 12+, signals 5/20, status read. Cinderella as a cyborg mechanic in a plague-struck New Beijing. I stamp it twelve-plus. Chaste romance, a plague that kills, and a stepmother who is cruel in modern ways.
- [The Selection by Kiera Cass](https://ripereads.example/books/the-selection/): ripe at 12+, signals 3/20, status read. The Bachelor in a caste-based monarchy, with a heroine who does not want to be there. I put it at twelve-plus; the romance is kisses and gowns, and the rebel attacks are the only menace.
- [Red Queen by Victoria Aveyard](https://ripereads.example/books/red-queen/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status read. Blood decides your caste; a Red girl turns out to have Silver powers. I put it at twelve-plus: the romance is kisses and betrayal, the violence is arena fights and executions.
- [Once Upon a Broken Heart by Stephanie Garber](https://ripereads.example/books/once-upon-a-broken-heart/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status read. A heartbroken girl makes a bargain with a Fate called Jacks, and the price is three kisses. Twelve-plus for me; sensual in language, chaste on the page, with a curse that turns kisses deadly.
- [The Inheritance Games by Jennifer Lynn Barnes](https://ripereads.example/books/the-inheritance-games/): ripe at 12+, signals 7/20, status read. A broke teenager inherits a billionaire's fortune and has to live in his puzzle-box mansion with his disinherited family. Not fantasy, but it is on every romantasy reader's list. Twelve-plus from me.
- [Divergent by Veronica Roth](https://ripereads.example/books/divergent/): ripe at 12+, signals 9/20, status read. Choose a faction, survive initiation, discover the system is rigged. Twelve-plus from me: the romance is kisses with one frank conversation about sex, and the initiation violence is rough.
- [The Maze Runner by James Dashner](https://ripereads.example/books/the-maze-runner/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status read. Boys in a glade, a maze that changes at night, monsters that sting. I stamp it twelve-plus; no romance to speak of, invented swearing, and a death toll that climbs.
- [Fable by Adrienne Young](https://ripereads.example/books/fable/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status read. A girl dumped on an island by her trader father claws her way back to sea. I put it at twelve-plus: a tight, salt-stained adventure with a slow romance and a brutal world kept mostly off the page.
- [Daughter of the Pirate King by Tricia Levenseller](https://ripereads.example/books/daughter-of-the-pirate-king/): ripe at 12+, signals 9/20, status read. A pirate captain gets herself captured on purpose to steal a map. I stamp it twelve-plus; swashbuckling, flirty and bloodier than the banter suggests, with a father who beats his daughter to toughen her.
- [Twilight by Stephenie Meyer](https://ripereads.example/books/twilight/): ripe at 12+, signals 5/20, status read. The book that built the genre's readership. I stamp it twelve-plus: resolutely chaste, mildly violent, and worth a conversation about a boyfriend who watches you sleep.
- [Rebel of the Sands by Alwyn Hamilton](https://ripereads.example/books/rebel-of-the-sands/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status read. A sharpshooting girl escapes a dead-end desert town with a mysterious foreigner and joins a rebellion. Twelve-plus from me: western pacing, djinn magic, a kissing romance and gunfights.
- [Raybearer by Jordan Ifueko](https://ripereads.example/books/raybearer/): ripe at 12+, signals 7/20, status read. A girl raised to kill the crown prince is sent to become one of his sworn council. I put it at twelve-plus: West African-inspired, morally rich, with a kissing romance and a plot built on child sacrifice.
- [Throne of Glass by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/throne-of-glass/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status read. An assassin is pulled from a death camp to compete for the job of king's champion. Book one is twelve-plus from me and chaste; by the series' end it is adult. I chart that drift because it is the question parents ask most about Maas.
- [Shatter Me by Tahereh Mafi](https://ripereads.example/books/shatter-me/): ripe at 14+, signals 8/20, status read. A girl whose touch kills is locked up by a regime that wants her as a weapon. I put it at fourteen-plus: the prose is strike-through and feverish, the romance is sensual, and the villain's obsession is uncomfortable on purpose.
- [Children of Blood and Bone by Tomi Adeyemi](https://ripereads.example/books/children-of-blood-and-bone/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. West African-inspired epic about bringing magic back to a kingdom that slaughtered its magic users. Fourteen-plus from me, on violence and an on-page allegory of police killings that is meant to hurt.
- [Sunrise on the Reaping by Suzanne Collins](https://ripereads.example/books/sunrise-on-the-reaping/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status read. Haymitch's Games, twenty-four years before Katniss. I stamp it fourteen-plus, a band above the original: the violence is more graphic, the aftermath is crueller, and Collins is writing about propaganda for a reader who has grown up.
- [Dance of Thieves by Mary E. Pearson](https://ripereads.example/books/dance-of-thieves/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. A reformed thief turned queen's soldier and the young leader of an outlaw dynasty, chained together and falling for each other. Fourteen-plus from me, on one steamy but non-explicit scene and routine frontier violence.
- [Heartless Hunter by Kristen Ciccarelli](https://ripereads.example/books/heartless-hunter/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status read. A witch in hiding dates the witch hunter who would burn her, to save a friend. I put it at fourteen-plus: the heat stays at heavy kissing, the purges are brutal, and the setup is Serpent & Dove with the door closed.
- [The Gilded Ones by Namina Forna](https://ripereads.example/books/the-gilded-ones/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status read. Girls who bleed gold are declared demons and killed, or recruited to fight for the empire that kills them. Fourteen-plus from me, on repeated violence against girls that the book is explicitly about.
- [Scythe by Neal Shusterman](https://ripereads.example/books/scythe/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status read. In a world without death, professional scythes kill to control population, and two teenagers are apprenticed to one. I stamp it fourteen-plus; no romance to speak of, but a mass killing and a cheerful sadist of an antagonist.
- [Reckless by Lauren Roberts](https://ripereads.example/books/reckless/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status read. The sequel to Powerless: Kai hunts Paedyn across the kingdom and neither of them means it. Fourteen-plus from me, same as the first; a little more violence, a little more heat, still closed-door.
- [Lore by Alexandra Bracken](https://ripereads.example/books/lore/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status read. Every seven years the Greek gods are made mortal and hunted through New York. I put it at fourteen-plus: bloody, propulsive, with a slow romance and a family massacre in the backstory.
- [Strange the Dreamer by Laini Taylor](https://ripereads.example/books/strange-the-dreamer/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status read. A junior librarian joins an expedition to a lost city where the children of murdered gods hide. Fourteen-plus from me: lyrical, slow, with a dreamy romance and a backstory of mass infanticide.
- [Legends & Lattes by Travis Baldree](https://ripereads.example/books/legends-and-lattes/): ripe at 14+, signals 6/20, status read. An orc mercenary retires to open a coffee shop. Adult-published and completely gentle; I stamp it fourteen-plus only because of a mild protection-racket plot and a sapphic romance that stays at kisses. A balm after anything on the 18+ shelf.
- [Assistant to the Villain by Hannah Nicole Maehrer](https://ripereads.example/books/assistant-to-the-villain/): ripe at 14+, signals 6/20, status read. A relentlessly cheerful woman takes an office job working for the kingdom's most feared villain. Adult-published rom-com with severed heads as decor. I put it at fourteen-plus; the romance is slow and chaste in this volume.
- [Iron Widow by Xiran Jay Zhao](https://ripereads.example/books/iron-widow/): ripe at 16+, signals 16/20, status read. Giant mechs piloted by boy-girl pairs, where the girls are expected to die. A furious feminist YA that I stamp sixteen-plus for sustained misogynistic violence, torture, and a polyamorous romance that stays non-explicit.
- [Kingdom of the Wicked by Kerri Maniscalco](https://ripereads.example/books/kingdom-of-the-wicked/): ripe at 16+, signals 12/20, status read. A witch in 1800s Sicily summons a prince of Hell to find her twin's killer. I put it at sixteen-plus: very sensual, with the sex arriving in book two, and ritual murders described in detail.
- [Girls of Paper and Fire by Natasha Ngan](https://ripereads.example/books/girls-of-paper-and-fire/): ripe at 16+, signals 12/20, status read. A girl taken as a concubine to a demon king falls in love with another of his Paper Girls. Sixteen-plus from me: an on-page sexual assault and the whole premise is sexual coercion, handled with care and an author's note.
- [The Night Circus by Erin Morgenstern](https://ripereads.example/books/the-night-circus/): ripe at 16+, signals 7/20, status read. Two magicians bound since childhood to a duel they do not understand, fought through a circus that opens only at night. Adult-published, very gentle; I stamp it sixteen-plus for one sensual scene and a slow pace that younger readers rarely finish.
- [The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue by V.E. Schwab](https://ripereads.example/books/the-invisible-life-of-addie-larue/): ripe at 16+, signals 11/20, status read. A woman makes a deal with the dark to live forever and is cursed to be forgotten by everyone she meets. Adult-published, enormously popular with teens. Sixteen-plus from me for on-page but non-graphic sex and a relationship with the devil that is frankly seductive.
- [A Court of Mist and Fury by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/a-court-of-mist-and-fury/): ripe at 18+, signals 13/20, status read. The book that turned a YA series into an adult one. Multiple long, explicit sex scenes and a frank treatment of trauma and an abusive relationship. I stamp it eighteen-plus; this is the volume parents mean when they ask whether ACOTAR is appropriate for a fourteen-year-old.
- [Iron Flame by Rebecca Yarros](https://ripereads.example/books/iron-flame/): ripe at 18+, signals 16/20, status read. Second year at Basgiath, with torture added to the curriculum. I stamp it eighteen-plus like its predecessor: the sex is explicit and frequent, the interrogation scenes are long, and nothing here is pitched younger.
- [Onyx Storm by Rebecca Yarros](https://ripereads.example/books/onyx-storm/): ripe at 18+, signals 16/20, status read. Third of the Empyrean: a quest across the sea for a cure, war at home, and a slightly lower heat than the first two. Still eighteen-plus from me; the explicit scenes are fewer but present, and the war violence is constant.
- [House of Earth and Blood by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/crescent-city-house-of-earth-and-blood/): ripe at 18+, signals 18/20, status read. Maas's first series published as adult from the start: a half-fae party girl and a fallen angel solve a murder in a modern fantasy city. Eighteen-plus from me, on explicit sex, heavy drug use and a graphic massacre.
- [From Blood and Ash by Jennifer L. Armentrout](https://ripereads.example/books/from-blood-and-ash/): ripe at 18+, signals 15/20, status read. A veiled Maiden, forbidden to be touched, and the guard assigned to protect her. The most common answer to 'what should my teen read after ACOTAR', and firmly eighteen-plus: explicit sex and a lot of it from the midpoint on.
- [Quicksilver by Callie Hart](https://ripereads.example/books/quicksilver/): ripe at 18+, signals 15/20, status read. A desert thief dragged into a fae court by a sardonic warrior. The 2024 breakout that teens found on TikTok. Eighteen-plus from me: explicit, extended sex scenes and pervasive strong language.
- [The Serpent and the Wings of Night by Carissa Broadbent](https://ripereads.example/books/the-serpent-and-the-wings-of-night/): ripe at 18+, signals 16/20, status read. A human raised by the vampire king enters a deadly tournament to earn immortality, and allies with a rival. Hunger Games with vampires and an adult romance. I stamp it eighteen-plus for explicit sex and graphic violence.
- [Ninth House by Leigh Bardugo](https://ripereads.example/books/ninth-house/): ripe at 18+, signals 17/20, status read. Bardugo's adult debut: Yale's secret societies do real magic, and a survivor of a drug-house massacre is hired to police them. Eighteen-plus from me, not for romance but for sexual assault, drug use and gore written without flinching. Six of Crows readers should know this is a different author.
- [Catching Fire by Suzanne Collins](https://ripereads.example/books/catching-fire/): ripe at 12+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. The second Hunger Games book keeps the first one's band. I stamp it twelve-plus: the arena is crueller and the state violence closer to home, but the romance stays at kisses and nothing is written for shock.
- [Mockingjay by Suzanne Collins](https://ripereads.example/books/mockingjay/): ripe at 14+, signals 12/20, status unmarked. The war book, and the one I move up a band. I stamp it fourteen-plus: the violence is sustained, a child's death lands as the book's turning point, and Katniss ends it with PTSD and a dependency on morphling. Brilliant, and bleak.
- [The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes by Suzanne Collins](https://ripereads.example/books/the-ballad-of-songbirds-and-snakes/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. The villain's origin story, and slower, colder and more philosophical than the trilogy. I stamp it fourteen-plus: the violence is less constant than Mockingjay but includes hangings and a murder by the narrator, and the reader is asked to sit inside the head of the man who becomes President Snow.
- [The Sea of Monsters by Rick Riordan](https://ripereads.example/books/percy-jackson-the-sea-of-monsters/): ripe at 10+, signals 2/20, status unmarked. A quest on the Odyssey's route with a Cyclops half-brother along for the ride. I stamp it ten-plus, same as The Lightning Thief: funny, fast and clean, with monster fights that end in golden dust rather than gore.
- [The Titan's Curse by Rick Riordan](https://ripereads.example/books/percy-jackson-the-titans-curse/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status unmarked. The winter book in the series, and the one with the first real losses. I keep it at ten-plus: two allies die, but off the page or gently, and the humour and pace never leave. Season 3 of the Disney+ show adapts it from November 20, 2026.
- [Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets by J.K. Rowling](https://ripereads.example/books/harry-potter-and-the-chamber-of-secrets/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status unmarked. Year two: a flying car, a monster in the pipes and a diary that writes back. I keep it at ten-plus with the first book. Scarier than Sorcerer's Stone in two set pieces, and the first book to name prejudice outright, but still well inside the band.
- [The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe by C.S. Lewis](https://ripereads.example/books/the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe/): ripe at 10+, signals 3/20, status unmarked. The winter where it is always winter and never Christmas, until it is. I stamp it ten-plus by this site's floor, but it is a read-aloud for six-year-olds and has been for seventy years. One sacrificial death, one battle, nothing more.
- [The Magician's Nephew by C.S. Lewis](https://ripereads.example/books/the-magicians-nephew/): ripe at 10+, signals 3/20, status unmarked. How Narnia began, and the book Greta Gerwig's film adapts in February 2027. I stamp it ten-plus by this site's floor; in practice it reads young. A dying mother and a dead world give it more weight than the cosy title suggests.
- [Wintersmith by Terry Pratchett](https://ripereads.example/books/wintersmith/): ripe at 10+, signals 5/20, status unmarked. A trainee witch dances into the dance of the seasons and Winter falls in love with her. The best winter fantasy on the middle-grade shelf, I think, and ten-plus from me: very funny, very wise and completely clean.
- [New Moon by Stephenie Meyer](https://ripereads.example/books/new-moon/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status unmarked. The breakup book. I keep it at twelve-plus with Twilight, but this is the volume where the themes signal rises: Bella's depression and her deliberate risk-taking are the core of the story, and a planned suicide drives the climax.
- [The Wicked King by Holly Black](https://ripereads.example/books/the-wicked-king/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status unmarked. Jude rules Faerie through a puppet king she cannot stop wanting. I stamp it fourteen-plus, like The Cruel Prince: the heat rises to one interrupted, non-explicit encounter, the violence is steady and the court is as drunk as ever.
- [The Queen of Nothing by Holly Black](https://ripereads.example/books/the-queen-of-nothing/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. The finale, and the volume that answers 'is the Cruel Prince series appropriate' for most families. I stamp it fourteen-plus: one fade-to-black sex scene, a war and a curse, and a satisfying ending.
- [Crown of Midnight by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/crown-of-midnight/): ripe at 14+, signals 10/20, status unmarked. The second Throne of Glass book, and where I start the series' climb. I stamp it fourteen-plus: a non-explicit sexual relationship, a friend's murder and Celaena's revenge give it more weight than the first book.
- [Ruthless Vows by Rebecca Ross](https://ripereads.example/books/ruthless-vows/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. The sequel to Divine Rivals, and the answer many readers want when they search for clean romantasy. I move it to fourteen-plus because the war is sharper and the married leads share a fade-to-black night; nothing is explicit.
- [Spinning Silver by Naomi Novik](https://ripereads.example/books/spinning-silver/): ripe at 14+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. A Rumpelstiltskin retelling set in an endless winter, adult-published and teen-friendly. I stamp it fourteen-plus: no sex on the page, but domestic abuse, antisemitism and a demon-possessed tsar give it weight.
- [The Bear and the Nightingale by Katherine Arden](https://ripereads.example/books/the-bear-and-the-nightingale/): ripe at 14+, signals 8/20, status unmarked. A Russian winter fairy tale for older readers. I stamp it fourteen-plus: little romance, but the dead rise, a stepmother descends into fear, and a priest's fixation on a teenage girl is menacing.
- [A Court of Wings and Ruin by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/a-court-of-wings-and-ruin/): ripe at 18+, signals 15/20, status unmarked. The war book of ACOTAR. I stamp it eighteen-plus: explicit sex scenes are fewer than in A Court of Mist and Fury but still there, and the battle violence is the series' heaviest.
- [A Court of Frost and Starlight by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/a-court-of-frost-and-starlight/): ripe at 18+, signals 12/20, status unmarked. The Winter Solstice novella, and the ACOTAR book searched most in December. I stamp it eighteen-plus: it is short and mostly gentle, but one explicit sex scene keeps it in the series' adult band.
- [A Court of Silver Flames by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/a-court-of-silver-flames/): ripe at 18+, signals 17/20, status unmarked. Nesta's book, and the most explicit in ACOTAR. I stamp it eighteen-plus without hesitation: frequent, long sex scenes and an addiction plot.
- [Alchemised by SenLinYu](https://ripereads.example/books/alchemised/): ripe at 18+, signals 17/20, status unmarked. The 2025 dark fantasy that teens are searching for by name. I stamp it eighteen-plus without hesitation: repeated non-consensual sex is the premise of the second act, and torture and suicide are on the page.
- [Dune by Frank Herbert](https://ripereads.example/books/dune/): ripe at 14+, signals 12/20, status unmarked. The desert planet, the spice and the boy who becomes a messiah. I stamp it fourteen-plus: almost no romance on the page and little bad language, but the villain is written as a predator of boys, the violence includes a child's death, and a drug runs the whole economy.
- [Dune Messiah by Frank Herbert](https://ripereads.example/books/dune-messiah/): ripe at 14+, signals 8/20, status unmarked. The short, bleak sequel that Dune: Part Three adapts on December 18, 2026. I stamp it fourteen-plus, like Dune: less fighting and no explicit content, but a holy war of billions, a blinding, a death in childbirth and an ending that walks into the desert.
- [A Christmas Carol by Charles Dickens](https://ripereads.example/books/a-christmas-carol/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status unmarked. Four ghosts, one miser and the best-known Christmas story in English. I stamp it ten-plus by this site's floor: nothing in it is unsuitable for a younger child, but the Victorian prose and two genuinely eerie ghosts make it a book to read aloud before ten.
- [The Hobbit by J.R.R. Tolkien](https://ripereads.example/books/the-hobbit/): ripe at 10+, signals 5/20, status unmarked. There and back again, with a dragon in the middle. I stamp it ten-plus: one battle, a few deaths and some genuinely creepy spiders, but no romance, no swearing and a narrator who talks to the reader like a grandparent by the fire.
- [Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban by J.K. Rowling](https://ripereads.example/books/harry-potter-and-the-prisoner-of-azkaban/): ripe at 10+, signals 6/20, status unmarked. The one with the Dementors, a werewolf teacher and a time-turner. I keep it at ten-plus, the last Harry Potter book I would put there: nobody dies, but the Dementors are the series' most frightening idea, and the backstory of Harry's parents' betrayal lands hard.
- [Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire by J.K. Rowling](https://ripereads.example/books/harry-potter-and-the-goblet-of-fire/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status unmarked. The Triwizard Tournament, the Yule Ball and the return of Voldemort. I move it up to twelve-plus: a student is murdered on the page, and the graveyard scene is the series' turning point from adventure to war.
- [The Battle of the Labyrinth by Rick Riordan](https://ripereads.example/books/percy-jackson-the-battle-of-the-labyrinth/): ripe at 10+, signals 4/20, status unmarked. The fourth Percy Jackson book: a maze under America, an inventor who never died and a war at camp. I keep it at ten-plus: deaths rise and the first kiss arrives, but the jokes and the bloodless monster fights hold.
- [A Good Girl's Guide to Murder by Holly Jackson](https://ripereads.example/books/a-good-girls-guide-to-murder/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status unmarked. A school project reopens a closed murder case. I stamp it fourteen-plus: no sex on the page, but a drug-facilitated rape is the key to the mystery, a dog is killed, and the teen party drinking and drug dealing are part of the investigation.
- [Red Rising by Pierce Brown](https://ripereads.example/books/red-rising/): ripe at 16+, signals 13/20, status unmarked. The Hunger Games with Roman legions on Mars, written for adults. I stamp it sixteen-plus. To answer the search directly: it is not spicy, but rape at the Institute is part of the plot, and the violence is the most brutal on this shelf below eighteen.
- [Mistborn: The Final Empire by Brandon Sanderson](https://ripereads.example/books/mistborn-the-final-empire/): ripe at 12+, signals 9/20, status unmarked. A heist against an immortal god-king, with magic you swallow. I stamp it twelve-plus: adult-published but written clean, with no sex and little swearing. The violence is real, and the empire's abuse of its enslaved people, including its women, is stated plainly.
- [Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir](https://ripereads.example/books/project-hail-mary/): ripe at 12+, signals 5/20, status unmarked. A science teacher wakes up alone in space and makes a friend. I stamp it twelve-plus: no romance and almost no violence; the swearing is the main reason it is not lower, and the joy of the science is why it is one of the easiest adult books to give a teen.
- [The Giver by Lois Lowry](https://ripereads.example/books/the-giver/): ripe at 12+, signals 8/20, status unmarked. The perfect community and the memory it erased. I stamp it twelve-plus: there is almost nothing on the surface, but the scene where Jonas watches his father 'release' a newborn is one of the most disturbing moments in middle-grade fiction, and it needs a grown-up nearby.
- [Heir of Fire by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/heir-of-fire/): ripe at 14+, signals 12/20, status unmarked. Celaena's grief book, and where the witches arrive. I stamp it fourteen-plus, like Crown of Midnight. To answer the search: it is not spicy; the heat is low. The violence and the witches' cruelty are what rise.
- [Queen of Shadows by Sarah J. Maas](https://ripereads.example/books/queen-of-shadows/): ripe at 16+, signals 14/20, status unmarked. Aelin comes home to settle her debts. I move the series up to sixteen-plus here: the sex is still behind the door, but the heat rises on the page, the violence is the series' most brutal yet, and the backstory of child sexual exploitation is spelled out.
- [Warriors: Into the Wild by Erin Hunter](https://ripereads.example/books/warriors-into-the-wild/): ripe at 10+, signals 3/20, status unmarked. A house cat joins a clan of wild warriors in the forest. I stamp it ten-plus: there is no romance or swearing, but cats fight to the death, and a senior warrior turns out to be a murderer. Warrior Cats is gentler than the battle scenes suggest and darker than the covers.
- [Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances by John Green, Maureen Johnson and Lauren Myracle](https://ripereads.example/books/let-it-snow/): ripe at 12+, signals 3/20, status unmarked. Three linked teen romances in one Christmas Eve blizzard. I stamp it twelve-plus: kisses, a snowbound Waffle House, cheerleaders and a teacup pig, with mild language and almost nothing else. The answer to 'clean Christmas books for teens'.
- [Dash & Lily's Book of Dares by Rachel Cohn and David Levithan](https://ripereads.example/books/dash-and-lilys-book-of-dares/): ripe at 14+, signals 7/20, status unmarked. A red notebook of dares left on a shelf at the Strand, passed back and forth across New York at Christmas. I stamp it fourteen-plus: the romance is sweet and the heat is low, but a party with underage drinking and some strong language put it a step above Let It Snow.
- [The Summer I Turned Pretty by Jenny Han](https://ripereads.example/books/the-summer-i-turned-pretty/): ripe at 12+, signals 6/20, status unmarked. A beach house, two brothers and the summer a girl turns sixteen. I stamp book one twelve-plus: kisses, one party with beer and a mother's illness. The series grows up fast, and the Prime Video show is older than book one, so check which a reader means.
- [The Name of the Wind by Patrick Rothfuss](https://ripereads.example/books/the-name-of-the-wind/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status unmarked. A legend tells his own story in an inn at the end of the world. I stamp it fourteen-plus: no sex and little swearing, but a massacre, years of homelessness as a child and a drug addiction plot sit inside a slow, beautiful book. The sequel climbs higher.
- [Crooked Kingdom by Leigh Bardugo](https://ripereads.example/books/crooked-kingdom/): ripe at 14+, signals 11/20, status unmarked. The Crows come home to Ketterdam to take revenge. I keep it at fourteen-plus with Six of Crows: kisses only, but the violence is steady, a drug runs through the plot, and Inej's trafficking and Kaz's trauma are at the centre.
